input.summary: Give Company convenience termination during an SOW; restrict Contractor's
input.comment: [Playbook] As drafted, neither party may terminate for convenience while a Statement of Work is open, so we are locked in, while Contractor can walk on 15 days' notice between SOWs. We need a 30-day convenience right (including for any SOW) with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, and Contractor should not be able to abandon an open Statement of Work for convenience.

ops.oldText: (a) At any time that there is no uncompleted Statement of Work outstanding, either party may terminate this Agreement for any or no reason upon fifteen (15) days advance notice to the other.
ops.newText: (a) Company may terminate this Agreement or any Statement of Work for convenience, in whole or in part, for any or no reason upon thirty (30) days advance written notice to Contractor, in which case Contractor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination and no early-termination fee or penalty shall be payable. At any time that there is no uncompleted Statement of Work outstanding, Contractor may terminate this Agreement for any or no reason upon ninety (90) days advance notice to Company.

input.summary: Move governing law and venue to New York courts
input.comment: [Playbook] Arizona law is outside our approved list (New York, Delaware, California, England and Wales), and disputes should go to courts rather than private arbitration under the USAM rules. We have set New York law with exclusive jurisdiction in New York County; Delaware or California would also work if Arizona is a problem for you.

ops.oldText: This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the Arizona, without regard to the conflict of laws provisions thereof.
ops.newText: This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of New York, without regard to the conflict of laws provisions thereof, and each party submits to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts located in New York County, New York.

ops.oldText: will be subject to and resolved by binding arbitration pursuant to the Arbitration Rules of U.S. Arbitration & Mediation, (www.usam.com).
ops.newText: will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts located in New York County, New York.
